daskin-vqpm-definition-ry: Section 2.1, p.4: the paper defines how VQPM turns power iteration into a variational circuit with Ry gates.
daskin-vqpm-definition-locking: Section 2.2, p.5: the paper defines the locking rule with the pdiff threshold.
daskin-vqpm-qpi-eigenvalue-range: Section 1.1, p.3: the paper states the assumption (eigenvalues in [0, pi/2]) and says 'In this paper, we have used [0, pi/2]'. A stated scope of its analysis.
daskin-vqpm-not-run-above-20: Section 2.2, p.6: the authors say they did not run n > 20; the 'likely needs more iterations' part is hedged in the value and in the text.
daskin-vqpm-degeneracy-not-checked: Section 3.1, p.7: the authors state they do not check for degenerate or close energies in their simulations.
daskin-vqpm-initial-state-fixed: Section 3.1, p.7: 'in our experiments we always use the equal superposition state as an initial state'.
daskin-vqpm-hoeffding-params: Section 3.2.3, p.10: M = 100 and delta_total = 0.5, with the factor 10n, chosen to keep eps in about [0.015, 0.005] for n <= 20, as the text states.
daskin-vqpm-qaoa-n8-setup: Figure 9 caption, p.13: 100 independent random QUBO trials at n = 8, VQPM pdiff 0.01, precision 3, 30 iterations; QAOA p = 8 with L-BFGS-B.
daskin-vqpm-hamming-vs-approx-ratio: Section 5, p.12 to 13: the text says it tracks Hamming distance, that alpha measures energy proximity, and that QAOA directly optimizes alpha while VQPM manipulates localized bit alignments.
daskin-vqpm-noise-setup: Section 6, p.14: Qiskit Aer noisy simulation with pdiff = 0.1 to limit noise impact on locking; the typical value is 0.01.
daskin-vqpm-future-work: Section 7, p.15: the authors name error-resilient dynamic locking thresholds and larger-scale problems as future research (open problems the paper states).
daskin-vqpm-ai-tools: Section 10, p.15: the acknowledgment says AI tools gave suggestions for the simulation code and the paper was proofread.
daskin-vqpm-table1-ranges: Table 1, p.18 to 19: the table lists the code parameters with typical ranges and 'precision 3 (best choice)'.
daskin-vqpm-setup: Figure 10 caption and Section 5, p.13: 10 trials per step, 30 iterations maximum, static pdiff = 0.01. Verified in both places.
dave-qnnp-architecture: Section II.C, p.4: angle embedding, three layers of RY and RX on each of four qubits, then CNOT entanglement.
dave-qnnq-architecture: Section II.E, p.5: two 2-qubit circuits with feature map and ansatz, EstimatorQNN module.
dave-qnnh-architecture: Section II.F, p.5: QNN-H joins a CNN with a QNN through TorchConnector.
dave-qnnp-loss-and-gradient: Section II.D, p.4 to 5: MSE loss on the Pauli-Z expectation, parameter-shift gradients, Adam optimizer (Eqs. 17 to 20).
dave-hyperparameters-adam: Section III.C, p.8: BCEWithLogitsLoss, Adam with beta1 = 0.9 and beta2 = 0.999 and a tuned learning rate.
dave-datasets: Section III.A, p.8: RODD and GPSD features as the value lists them.
dave-preprocessing-balance: Section III.B, p.8: PCA or feature selection, equal label balance in training, StandardScaler.
dave-noise-param-range: Section III.E, p.8: noise parameter spectrum 0 to 1.
dave-noise-models-six: Section II.G, p.5: six noise models; the passage lists bit flip, phase flip, bit phase flip, depolarizing, phase damping and amplitude damping.
dave-qnnp-only-noise-scope: Section III.E, p.9: the authors state noise analysis covers QNN-P only and give their reason.
dave-future-research: Section IV, p.10: future research on tensor networks, quantum error mitigation and larger datasets, as the paper states.
dave-setup-simulation-300-points: Section I and Section IV: simulation experiments on two datasets, metrics for 300 data points (Section IV, p.10 states 300).

deborba-kernel-is-measured-value: Metodologia, p.5: the kernel is the measured value; the rendered page shows k = |<x_i|x_j>|^2, as the value says.
deborba-block-construction: Metodologia, p.6 to 7: the paper defines its block construction, pairs of coefficients and a control coefficient.
deborba-angle-caveat: Metodologia, p.8: the paper states that the order of operators matters, that the angle equations can fail in some cases, and that sequences and angles must be chosen case by case.
deborba-software-setup: Resultados, p.9: Python, NumPy, Qiskit 0.16.1 on Google Colab, as the passage states.
deborba-noiseless-simulator: Resultados, p.9: statevector_simulator, no noise, ideal circuit.
deborba-data-setup: Resultados, p.9: square side 1.08, circle radius 0.42, classes by outside or inside.
deborba-radius-forgotten: Resultados, p.9: 'o raio e esquecido' after the ideal outputs are set.
deborba-offset-computed: Resultados, p.9: an offset was computed from the training set and used for 100 new random points.
deborba-limit-noise-hardware: Conclusoes, p.10: current hardware noise is too high for experimental verification; only ideal-case simulation was run. The passage also names noisy simulators as future work.
deborba-limit-classical-optimizations: Conclusoes, p.10: the authors name classical-side optimizations (a hybrid kernel algorithm for more general situations) as not yet done.
deborba-kernel-scope: English abstract, p.11: proposes a hybrid method based on classic kernels and tests it on the inside-or-outside-circle problem; scope as the authors state it.
defelice-prop-2-3-type-i-kraus: Proposition 2.3, Section 2.5, p.9: stated with its conditions (CP interpretation, s = a xor b) and proved by the explicit QPath computation in Appendix B, p.43 to 45; no cited theorem is a step.
defelice-green-failure-definition: Definition 3.2, Section 3.2, p.15: the paper defines green failure.
defelice-prop-3-3-green-failure-form: Proposition 3.3, Section 3.2, p.15: stated with conditions and derived in the preceding text by the Euler decomposition and the beta_i case analysis (Eq. 11). No separate Proof block, and the diagrams were not viewed; no cited theorem is used.
defelice-prop-3-5-green-pauli-form: Proposition 3.5, Section 3.3, p.16: stated with conditions and proved in Appendix C, p.46 by a commutation argument on phi; no cited theorem is a step.
defelice-theorem-3-8-symmetric-form: Theorem 3.8, Section 3.3, p.16: stated with conditions; the paper's proof is one line from Proposition 3.5 (proved in Appendix C). The symmetry step is not shown, only asserted to follow directly.
defelice-prop-3-14-x-or-y: Proposition 3.14, Section 3.4, p.17 to 18: follows from Theorem 3.8 with alpha a multiple of pi/2 by the case split on a = alpha/(pi/2) given in the text just before it. No Proof block; no cited theorem is a step.
defelice-def-xy-flow: Definition 4.13, Section 4.3, p.22: the paper defines XY-flow.
defelice-pattern-corrections-limit: Remark 4.10, Section 4.2, p.21: the definition assumes corrections only on register qubits, so none on fusion nodes; a more refined pattern may be needed for other fusions.
defelice-def-pauli-flow: Definition 2.13, Section 2.8, p.13: the nine conditions are stated; the paper states the definition it uses (from [10, 36]).
defelice-def-determinism: Section 2.7, p.12: the paper defines deterministic and strongly deterministic patterns.
defelice-dual-rail-remark: Remark 2.2, Section 2.3, p.7: results focus on dual-rail qubits; only the equations of that subsection are used.
defelice-lemma-5-4-permutation: Lemma 5.4, Section 5.2, p.27 to 28: stated with the setup and proved constructively by giving the control streams x_t and y_t. The proof is only the construction; the router diagram was not viewed. No cited theorem is a step.
defelice-def-unrolling: Definition 5.3, Section 5.1, p.26: the paper defines unrolling.
defelice-theorem-6-4-prob: Theorem 6.4, Section 6.2, p.33: stated for n >= 1 and proved by induction in Appendix E from Proposition 6.2 and Equation (22); the probability 1 - 1/2^(n+1) follows from the stated equation. No cited theorem is a step.
defelice-universality-assumptions: Section 6.3, p.34: the paper lists three idealising assumptions and leaves their relaxation to future work.
defelice-compilation-scope: Section 1, p.4: the authors state their focus is the formal description, not optimization, left to future work.
defelice-future-optimisation: Section 7, p.36: the passage names fusion-count minimisation and photon-loss reduction as further development; both parts of the value are in the passage.
xy-flow-only-x-and-y-fusions: Section 7, p.36: the conclusion states the flow is developed for X and Y fusions only and leaves more general fusions to future work.
